historical_context.narrative: Threshold Schnorr implementations often relied on fresh randomized nonces, preprocessed state, or careful continuity of state across sessions. Garillot, Kondi, Mohassel, and Nikolaenko pursued a different operational contract: deterministic nonce derivation without evolving signer state. TSIG-RESULT-1989-DF-DISTRIBUTED-RSA-SIGN.label: Distributed RSA signing
TSIG-RESULT-1989-DF-DISTRIBUTED-RSA-SIGN.lane_rationale: Instantiates the threshold paradigm by distributing RSA private exponentiation rather than defining a separate notion.
TSIG-RESULT-1989-DF-DISTRIBUTED-RSA-SIGN.selection_rationale: Shows the early RSA instantiation of the threshold paradigm; it remains related because GJKR and Shoup supply the robust, operationally sharper RSA lineage.

TSIG-RESULT-1989-DF-THRESHOLD-CRYPTOSYST.label: Distributed private-key operations
TSIG-RESULT-1989-DF-THRESHOLD-CRYPTOSYST.lane_rationale: Formulates quorum-controlled private-key operations as the threshold-cryptosystem research interface, without claiming modern robustness for all instantiations.
TSIG-RESULT-1989-DF-THRESHOLD-CRYPTOSYST.selection_rationale: Preserves the original quorum-service boundary for private-key operations; bibliographic-level evidence and later robustness refinements keep it beside, rather than on, the default backbone.

TSIG-RESULT-1991-PEDERSEN-DISTRIBUTED-KE.label: Dealerless discrete-log DKG
TSIG-RESULT-1991-PEDERSEN-DISTRIBUTED-KE.lane_rationale: Provides a dealerless discrete-log key-generation protocol as an independently reusable setup mechanism.
TSIG-RESULT-1991-PEDERSEN-DISTRIBUTED-KE.selection_rationale: Keeps dealerless discrete-log setup visible as an independent component; the later GJKR result carries the robust malicious-minority transition on the backbone.

TSIG-RESULT-1996-GJKR-DSS-ROBUST-THRESHO.label: Robust threshold DSS
TSIG-RESULT-1996-GJKR-DSS-ROBUST-THRESHO.lane_rationale: Constructs threshold DSS with ordinary verification output and the paper's scoped resilience bound.
TSIG-RESULT-1996-GJKR-DSS-ROBUST-THRESHO.selection_rationale: Retains the first robust treatment of DSS's nonlinear signing equation without implying a generic compiler; its exact resilience bound is part of the contribution.

TSIG-RESULT-1996-GJKR-RSA-ROBUST-THRESHO.label: Robust RSA function sharing
TSIG-RESULT-1996-GJKR-RSA-ROBUST-THRESHO.lane_rationale: Gives verifiable robust sharing of RSA private operations under its stated setup and resilience conditions.
TSIG-RESULT-1996-GJKR-RSA-ROBUST-THRESHO.selection_rationale: Records the robust RSA-function-sharing baseline from which Shoup simplifies the signing path; bibliographic-level locators keep it as reviewed context.

TSIG-RESULT-1999-GJKR-DKG-ROBUST-DISCRET.label: Robust discrete-log DKG
TSIG-RESULT-1999-GJKR-DKG-ROBUST-DISCRET.lane_rationale: Supplies the robust malicious-party DKG protocol, a setup mechanism separable from any one signing scheme.
TSIG-RESULT-1999-GJKR-DKG-ROBUST-DISCRET.selection_rationale: Marks the point where dealerless key generation becomes a robust malicious-party protocol and an auditable component separable from any one signature scheme.

TSIG-RESULT-2000-SHOUP-NONINTERACTIVE-SH.label: Noninteractive RSA signature shares
TSIG-RESULT-2000-SHOUP-NONINTERACTIVE-SH.lane_rationale: Reduces the post-setup signing-share interaction requirement by allowing independent share production and checking; setup is explicitly excluded.
TSIG-RESULT-2000-SHOUP-NONINTERACTIVE-SH.selection_rationale: Separates Shoup's post-setup noninteractive share path from the complete scheme, preventing the online round claim from silently including key generation.

TSIG-RESULT-2000-SHOUP-PRACTICAL-ROBUST-.label: Verifiable-share threshold RSA
TSIG-RESULT-2000-SHOUP-PRACTICAL-ROBUST-.lane_rationale: Gives a complete robust RSA threshold-signature construction with publicly verifiable shares and ordinary RSA output.
TSIG-RESULT-2000-SHOUP-PRACTICAL-ROBUST-.selection_rationale: Anchors the mature threshold-RSA branch with a complete robust scheme, publicly checkable shares, and ordinary RSA output rather than only an early distributed exponentiation idea.

TSIG-RESULT-2003-BOLDYREVA-THRESHOLD-BLS.label: Threshold BLS
TSIG-RESULT-2003-BOLDYREVA-THRESHOLD-BLS.lane_rationale: Constructs threshold BLS by exponent sharing and combination of partial signatures without reconstructing the private key.
TSIG-RESULT-2003-BOLDYREVA-THRESHOLD-BLS.selection_rationale: Opens the pairing branch with exponent-share threshold BLS; its one-element ordinary-verifier output is kept as a neighboring capability rather than folded into the mechanism.

TSIG-RESULT-2017-LINDELL-EFFICIENT-TWO-P.label: Paillier-based two-party ECDSA
TSIG-RESULT-2017-LINDELL-EFFICIENT-TWO-P.lane_rationale: Provides a concrete Paillier-based two-party protocol yielding an ordinary ECDSA signature, not a general t-out-of-n scheme.
TSIG-RESULT-2017-LINDELL-EFFICIENT-TWO-P.selection_rationale: Establishes the Paillier-based two-party ECDSA baseline with ordinary verifier output; later multiparty work changes the participant setting rather than replacing this starting point.

TSIG-RESULT-2018-DKLS-2P-HASH-PROOF-SYST.label: HPS-based ECDSA multiplication
TSIG-RESULT-2018-DKLS-2P-HASH-PROOF-SYST.lane_rationale: Isolates the reusable HPS-based correlated-computation mechanism used in the ECDSA multiplication step.
TSIG-RESULT-2018-DKLS-2P-HASH-PROOF-SYST.selection_rationale: Isolates the hash-proof-system multiplication component so readers do not mistake the phrase Paillier-free for setup-free or for a complete scheme mechanism by itself.

TSIG-RESULT-2018-DKLS-2P-TWO-PARTY-ECDSA.label: Paillier-free two-party ECDSA
TSIG-RESULT-2018-DKLS-2P-TWO-PARTY-ECDSA.lane_rationale: Constructs two-party ECDSA using the HPS/OT route instead of Paillier multiplication, without implying setup-free or assumption-free signing.
TSIG-RESULT-2018-DKLS-2P-TWO-PARTY-ECDSA.selection_rationale: Preserves the Paillier-free ECDSA route as a serious alternative assumption stack; it remains related because the main ECDSA backbone follows the Paillier-to-multiparty transition.

TSIG-RESULT-2018-GG-DISTRIBUTED-SETUP.label: Dealerless ECDSA setup
TSIG-RESULT-2018-GG-DISTRIBUTED-SETUP.lane_rationale: Provides dealerless setup of the distributed ECDSA key material as a distinct protocol component.
TSIG-RESULT-2018-GG-DISTRIBUTED-SETUP.selection_rationale: Keeps trustless key generation beside GG18's multiparty signing result, making clear that dealerless setup is a component and not the later proactive-refresh guarantee.

TSIG-RESULT-2018-GG-MULTIPARTY-THRESHOLD.label: Multiparty threshold ECDSA
TSIG-RESULT-2018-GG-MULTIPARTY-THRESHOLD.lane_rationale: Realizes multiparty threshold ECDSA beyond the two-party setting while preserving ordinary verification output.
TSIG-RESULT-2018-GG-MULTIPARTY-THRESHOLD.selection_rationale: Marks the participant-model transition from two parties to a genuine t-out-of-n ECDSA protocol while keeping the ordinary verification interface unchanged.

TSIG-RESULT-2019-DKLS-N-GENERAL-THRESHOL.label: General Paillier-free threshold ECDSA
TSIG-RESULT-2019-DKLS-N-GENERAL-THRESHOL.lane_rationale: Extends the Paillier-free route to a general threshold protocol; the broad bibliographic claim is retained without new exact theorem or performance coordinates.
TSIG-RESULT-2019-DKLS-N-GENERAL-THRESHOL.selection_rationale: Extends the alternative DKLS assumption route to general quorums; bibliographic-level evidence keeps it reviewed-related and prevents unsupported UC or performance comparisons.

TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-IDENTIFIABLE-ABOR.label: Identifiable ECDSA abort
TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-IDENTIFIABLE-ABOR.lane_rationale: Provides the protocol's accountable-abort mechanism identifying a misbehaving participant, without treating blame as liveness.
TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-IDENTIFIABLE-ABOR.selection_rationale: Records accountable failure without implying liveness; it remains related because the UC security treatment carries the paper's primary map position.

TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-ONE-MESSAGE-DEPEN.label: One online CGGMP round
TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-ONE-MESSAGE-DEPEN.lane_rationale: Moves message-independent work to preprocessing so only one signing round depends on the message, without claiming one round end to end.
TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-ONE-MESSAGE-DEPEN.selection_rationale: Separates message-dependent latency from the paper's UC theorem; it stays related because the complete protocol still includes a multi-round preprocessing phase.

TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-PROACTIVE-SECURIT.label: Proactive ECDSA share refresh
TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-PROACTIVE-SECURIT.lane_rationale: Implements share renewal across epochs while retaining the verification key; the refresh mechanism depends on explicit erasure and corruption conditions.
TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-PROACTIVE-SECURIT.selection_rationale: Makes epoch-based share refresh visible as a lifecycle guarantee, while keeping its erasure and corruption assumptions separate from the core UC-signing claim.

TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-UC-THRESHOLD-ECDS.label: Adaptive UC threshold ECDSA
TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-UC-THRESHOLD-ECDS.lane_rationale: Realizes threshold ECDSA with adaptive UC security in the global random-oracle model; the security advance belongs to the stronger-secure protocol rather than a generic assumption label.
TSIG-RESULT-2020-CGGMP-UC-THRESHOLD-ECDS.selection_rationale: Marks the composable-security transition for practical multiparty ECDSA; preprocessing, proactive refresh, and blame remain separately inspectable coordinates rather than one compound label.

TSIG-RESULT-2020-FROST-ONE-ROUND-WITH-PR.label: One online FROST round
TSIG-RESULT-2020-FROST-ONE-ROUND-WITH-PR.lane_rationale: Reduces message-dependent online interaction to one round using fresh preprocessed nonces, with preprocessing still counted separately.
TSIG-RESULT-2020-FROST-ONE-ROUND-WITH-PR.selection_rationale: Preserves the latency optimization while stating its accounting boundary explicitly; one online round must not be presented as one round end to end.

TSIG-RESULT-2020-FROST-TWO-ROUND-THRESHO.label: Two-round t-out-of-n FROST
TSIG-RESULT-2020-FROST-TWO-ROUND-THRESHO.lane_rationale: Defines the complete two-round t-out-of-n Schnorr signing workflow, keeping the nonce-preprocessing latency result separate.
TSIG-RESULT-2020-FROST-TWO-ROUND-THRESHO.selection_rationale: Anchors the Schnorr branch with a true t-out-of-n two-round signing workflow; preprocessing and malformed-share handling remain separate neighboring contributions.

TSIG-RESULT-2021-DOTT-ABORT-LEAKAGE-COUN.label: Abort-leakage trapdoor commitments
TSIG-RESULT-2021-DOTT-ABORT-LEAKAGE-COUN.lane_rationale: Provides the homomorphic trapdoor-commitment countermeasure that protects the DOTT protocol's abort transcripts, not a generic impossibility or security analysis.
TSIG-RESULT-2021-DOTT-ABORT-LEAKAGE-COUN.selection_rationale: Makes abort leakage a first-class security problem and records DOTT's protocol-specific repair; it remains related because it is a component of the complete construction.

TSIG-RESULT-2021-DOTT-TWO-ROUND-N-OUT-OF.label: Two-round n-out-of-n lattice signing
TSIG-RESULT-2021-DOTT-TWO-ROUND-N-OUT-OF.lane_rationale: Gives a concrete two-round lattice signing protocol for full n-out-of-n participation, not arbitrary threshold participation.
TSIG-RESULT-2021-DOTT-TWO-ROUND-N-OUT-OF.selection_rationale: Establishes two-round lattice Fiat–Shamir-with-aborts signing at the n-out-of-n boundary, giving later arbitrary-threshold work a precise starting point.

TSIG-RESULT-2021-GKMN-STATELESS-DETERMIN.label: Stateless deterministic threshold Schnorr
TSIG-RESULT-2021-GKMN-STATELESS-DETERMIN.lane_rationale: Builds deterministic stateless threshold Schnorr using nonce-generation and proof machinery, realizing a distinct operational contract.
TSIG-RESULT-2021-GKMN-STATELESS-DETERMIN.selection_rationale: Marks a different operational contract for dishonest-majority Schnorr signing, replacing fresh randomness and evolving state with deterministic nonce machinery.

TSIG-RESULT-2022-DILIZIUM2-TWO-PARTY-DIL.label: Three-round two-party Dilithium
TSIG-RESULT-2022-DILIZIUM2-TWO-PARTY-DIL.lane_rationale: Constructs the audited three-round two-party DOTT-related protocol with Dilithium compression; its outdated preprint and limited party setting remain explicit.
TSIG-RESULT-2022-DILIZIUM2-TWO-PARTY-DIL.selection_rationale: Keeps the full-text-audited three-round two-party Dilithium-oriented point visible without promoting it to arbitrary-threshold or ML-DSA compatibility; the available ePrint is explicitly outdated relative to the journal version.

TSIG-RESULT-2023-GKS-ACTIVELY-SECURE-THR.label: Actively secure threshold linear HE
TSIG-RESULT-2023-GKS-ACTIVELY-SECURE-THR.lane_rationale: Provides the actively secure threshold-LHE aggregation layer as an independently meaningful signing component.
TSIG-RESULT-2023-GKS-ACTIVELY-SECURE-THR.selection_rationale: Keeps the actively secure linear-HE layer independently inspectable so the GKS threshold generalization is not misread as avoiding homomorphic machinery.

TSIG-RESULT-2023-GKS-TWO-ROUND-ARBITRARY.label: Two-round t-out-of-n lattice signing
TSIG-RESULT-2023-GKS-TWO-ROUND-ARBITRARY.lane_rationale: Realizes arbitrary t-out-of-n lattice signing in two rounds through threshold linear HE, a new construction setting rather than unconditional efficiency dominance.
TSIG-RESULT-2023-GKS-TWO-ROUND-ARBITRARY.selection_rationale: Marks the shift from DOTT's full participation to arbitrary t-out-of-n signing while retaining two rounds, with threshold linear HE made explicit as the enabling cost.

TSIG-RESULT-2023-OLAF-PROOF-WITHOUT-AGM.label: FROST proof without AGM
TSIG-RESULT-2023-OLAF-PROOF-WITHOUT-AGM.lane_rationale: The principal contribution is a FROST-variant unforgeability analysis without AGM, retaining AOMDL and the random-oracle model.
TSIG-RESULT-2023-OLAF-PROOF-WITHOUT-AGM.selection_rationale: Represents the proof-model transition away from AGM for a FROST-style protocol while leaving AOMDL and the random oracle visible as the replacement assumptions.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-AOMMLWE-OFFLINE-ONLINE-.label: Signer-independent offline lattice phase
TSIG-RESULT-2024-AOMMLWE-OFFLINE-ONLINE-.lane_rationale: Makes the first round independent of both message and signer set to reduce online completion work, without removing total offline interaction.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-AOMMLWE-OFFLINE-ONLINE-.selection_rationale: Separates signer-set- and message-independent preprocessing from the complete two-round scheme so online latency is not confused with total interaction.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-AOMMLWE-TWO-ROUND-LATTI.label: Two-round lattice signing without FHE
TSIG-RESULT-2024-AOMMLWE-TWO-ROUND-LATTI.lane_rationale: Constructs two-round threshold lattice signing without FHE or homomorphic trapdoor commitments, under the explicit adaptive AOM-MLWE assumption.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-AOMMLWE-TWO-ROUND-LATTI.selection_rationale: Anchors the two-round lattice route that avoids FHE and homomorphic trapdoor commitments, while exposing AOM-MLWE rather than suggesting an assumption-free simplification.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-FLOOD-FIRST-HASH-AND-SI.label: Lattice threshold hash-and-sign
TSIG-RESULT-2024-FLOOD-FIRST-HASH-AND-SI.lane_rationale: Constructs a robust distributed GPV-style hash-and-sign protocol rather than a universal compiler for every lattice signature.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-FLOOD-FIRST-HASH-AND-SI.selection_rationale: Opens a lattice hash-and-sign threshold branch distinct from abort-based designs; the distributed short-secret tools are kept as companion mechanisms.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-FLOOD-RANDOM-SUBMERSION.label: Random-submersion short-share proofs
TSIG-RESULT-2024-FLOOD-RANDOM-SUBMERSION.lane_rationale: Supplies the random-submersion mechanism for verifiable sharing of short lattice secrets, with noise flooding and parameters retained.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-FLOOD-RANDOM-SUBMERSION.selection_rationale: Records the short-share verification mechanism required by Flood and Submerse without presenting it as either a complete DKG or a standalone signature.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-GLACIUS-FULLY-ADAPTIVE-.label: Fully adaptive DDH threshold Schnorr
TSIG-RESULT-2024-GLACIUS-FULLY-ADAPTIVE-.lane_rationale: Provides the stronger-secure threshold Schnorr protocol achieving full adaptivity from DDH in the ROM with identifiable abort; it is not only a reproof of an unchanged protocol.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-GLACIUS-FULLY-ADAPTIVE-.selection_rationale: Marks the corruption-timing frontier for threshold Schnorr by combining full t<n adaptivity from DDH in the ROM with constant-size signing keys and identifiable abort.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-RACCOON-EFFICIENT-LARGE.label: Three-round lattice signing through T=1024
TSIG-RESULT-2024-RACCOON-EFFICIENT-LARGE.lane_rationale: Establishes a contextual concrete size-and-scale point through threshold 1024 with a three-round profile, not a normalized cross-paper benchmark ranking.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-RACCOON-EFFICIENT-LARGE.selection_rationale: Anchors the practical standard-lattice scale point with a full-text-audited three-round protocol, concrete T=1024 parameters, and implementation tables; trusted KeyGen and non-robust abort behavior remain explicit coordinates.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-RACCOON-ONE-TIME-ADDITI.label: Additive-mask abort-leakage defense
TSIG-RESULT-2024-RACCOON-ONE-TIME-ADDITI.lane_rationale: Introduces the session-unique pairwise additive-mask mechanism preventing accumulated partial-signature leakage, with mask non-reuse conditions explicit.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-RACCOON-ONE-TIME-ADDITI.selection_rationale: Exposes the full-text-audited pairwise one-time-mask mechanism behind Raccoon's scale claim; it remains related because session-unique PRF masking is a component, not a generic repair for all lattice threshold signatures.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-TANG-FUNCTIONAL-INTERCH.label: Ordinary-verifier lattice threshold signing
TSIG-RESULT-2024-TANG-FUNCTIONAL-INTERCH.lane_rationale: Constructs threshold lattice signing whose output follows the selected ordinary scheme's verification interface, without asserting ML-DSA compatibility.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-TANG-FUNCTIONAL-INTERCH.selection_rationale: Anchors ordinary-verifier interchangeability with full-text evidence that DSign outputs the base scheme's conventional signature format and that key/signature sizes are independent of the participant count; this remains distinct from ML-DSA compatibility.

TSIG-RESULT-2024-TANG-PROACTIVE-REFRESH.label: Proactive lattice share refresh
TSIG-RESULT-2024-TANG-PROACTIVE-REFRESH.lane_rationale: Provides a proactive lattice share-renewal procedure preserving the public key under the paper's epoch and corruption model.
TSIG-RESULT-2024-TANG-PROACTIVE-REFRESH.selection_rationale: Keeps Theorem 2's proactive share renewal as a lifecycle coordinate rather than merging it with construction or interoperability; the at-most-t-1 corruption bound per refresh period remains explicit.

problems.label: Adaptive corruption security
problems.question: Which protocols remain secure when the adversary chooses corruptions during execution rather than fixing them in advance?

problems.label: Proof models and assumptions
problems.question: Which proof-model or hardness assumptions underwrite deployable threshold signing, and what changes when one is removed?

problems.label: Malicious robustness and blame
problems.question: How do protocols preserve consistency or identify deviators when participants submit malformed setup or signing shares?

problems.label: Abort-leakage security
problems.question: How do lattice protocols prevent repeated partial signatures and abort transcripts from leaking distributed signing secrets?

problems.label: Post-quantum thresholding
problems.question: How can lattice signing tolerate distributed secrets, abort leakage, and arbitrary thresholds?

problems.label: Interoperable output and evaluation
problems.question: Which results preserve ordinary verification and support comparable, swappable threshold packages?

relations.evidence_locator: GJKR CRYPTO 1996 paper, overview and robustness sections
relations.statement: GJKR develops the shared-RSA branch with verifiable shares and robustness against malicious behavior rather than only distributing the private operation.
GJKR realizes quorum-controlled signing for the DSS signing equation, producing ordinary DSS signatures with the construction's stated resilience and robustness conditions.

Relative to early distributed RSA private operations, Shoup gives a robust signing construction whose servers independently produce publicly checkable shares after setup; this does not compare total key-generation costs.

relations.evidence_locator: Shoup related-work comparison and construction overview
relations.statement: Shoup presents a more practical robust threshold-RSA signature protocol with noninteractive signature shares and direct share verification.

relations.evidence_locator: GJKR DKG abstract, introduction, and protocol comparison
relations.statement: GJKR revisits discrete-log DKG and supplies a robust malicious-security treatment for distributed key generation.

relations.evidence_locator: GG18 abstract, introduction, and prior-work comparison
relations.statement: GG18 moves the practical Paillier-based ECDSA line from two parties to a general multiparty threshold setting with distributed setup.

relations.evidence_locator: IEEE paper abstract and construction overview
relations.statement: The later DKLS threshold construction generalizes the two-party OT/hash-proof-system route to a general threshold protocol.

relations.evidence_locator: CGGMP revised full version, abstract and contribution overview
relations.statement: Building on GG18, CGGMP strengthens the practical multiparty-ECDSA line with an adaptive UC treatment in the global random-oracle model.

relations.evidence_locator: CGGMP revised full version, abstract and contribution overview
relations.statement: Building on GG18, CGGMP moves all message-independent signing rounds into preprocessing and leaves one message-dependent online round.

relations.evidence_locator: FROST Sections 2.3 and 5.1, Figure 1, PDF pp. 6–10
relations.statement: FROST can be composed with a discrete-log DKG to create the shared Schnorr key, while its paper focuses on round-optimized signing.
Olaf combines the efficient FROST3 variant with a Pedersen-DKG variant and proves unforgeability without the algebraic group model.
Glacius changes the security point to fully adaptive corruptions from DDH while retaining compact Schnorr output and adding a formal identifiable-abort guarantee.

relations.evidence_locator: DiLizium 2.0 Sections 1.1–1.2, PDF pp. 2–3; audited ePrint is marked outdated
relations.statement: DiLizium 2.0 follows the DOTT commitment-based logic but incorporates Dilithium signature-compression techniques in a two-party authentication setting.

relations.evidence_locator: GKS Section 5, Figure 7 and Theorem 3, PDF pp. 22–26
relations.statement: GKS preserves two signing rounds while moving from DOTT's full n-out-of-n threshold to arbitrary t<=n through threshold linearly homomorphic encryption.

relations.evidence_locator: Threshold Raccoon Section 1.1, PDF pp. 4–5; Sections 2.3 and 6; Tables 2–3, PDF pp. 8–10, 20–23, and 43–44
relations.statement: Threshold Raccoon trades DOTT's two-round homomorphic-trapdoor-commitment route for a three-round, pairwise-mask design with concrete parameter sets through T=1024.

relations.evidence_locator: AOM-MLWE Sections 1.1, 2.1, and 6.2, Figures 2 and 8, Theorem 6.1, PDF pp. 4–10 and 33–36
relations.statement: Starting from Threshold Raccoon's pairwise-mask approach, the AOM-MLWE construction reduces signing from three rounds to two and makes the first round message- and signer-set-independent by introducing an algebraic one-more lattice assumption.
